title: LTS channel blueprint and automated upgrade guardrail spec for runtime/API/SDK/Console
creator: Aisha Tan
description: Goal: Produce a single-source blueprint and implementation plan for Redwood's LTS channels that covers versioning semantics and compatibility guarantees across the serving runtime, public API, SDKs, and Console. Deliver a machine-readable compatibility map, set of automated rollout gates, and a minimal upgrade tooling prototype (CLI + CI validators) so teams can safely pin to LTS releases and perform staged upgrades with confidence. Scope includes: runtime binary and model-serving contract compatibility, API semantic versioning policy, SDK runtime checks and feature flags, Console compatibility shims and telemetry hooks, upgrade validation CI jobs, and rollback choreography. Out of scope: full automated multi-region canary orchestration (follow-up work).
acceptance_criteria: Publish LTS blueprint doc with versioning rules and compatibility guarantees for runtime/API/SDK/Console
Provide a JSON compatibility map (machine-readable) that lists supported cross-surface pairings and allowed minor/patch divergences
Implement 2 CI validators: (1) compatibility-check against the map; (2) smoke test suite that exercises critical APIs and runtime startup under new LTS versions
Define automated rollout gates (health, error-rate, perf delta thresholds, telemetry sanity checks) encoded as policy rules
Prototype an upgrade CLI that can: run pre-upgrade checks, tag a deployment with an LTS channel, and trigger a staged rollout via the Console API
Document rollback criteria and automated unwind steps for a failed staged upgrade
Obtain engineering lead sign-off and Security review approval

design_notes: Versioning model: adopt 'channel.major.minor' human-readable tags. LTS channels pinned to major with rolling minor security/patches. Example: lts-2.1. Allowed upgrade path: patch auto-apply, minor via gated canary, major via scheduled migration and explicit opt-in.
Compatibility map format: flat list of rules. Each rule is a triple: (surface_a, surface_b, compatibility_range). The CI validator will fail merges that introduce map contradictions.

Rollout gates: implement policy DSL with the following checks: health_slope (service-level error rate delta), p95_latency_delta, model_quality_regression (via eval set), logging_sanity (no missing traces), and disk/memory pressure thresholds. Policies return PASS/WARN/FAIL for automation.

Upgrade tooling: minimal CLI that performs dry-run checks, posts results to a central rollout log, and can create a canary cohort via Console API. CLI uses the compatibility map to validate requested channel pairings before proceeding.

Rollback choreography: immediate stop of rollout + automated revert to last known-good artifact; post-mortem checklist triggers and incident channel creation; collector collects telemetry snapshot for the failed window.
Telemetry requirements: add new rollout tags to traces, capture per-channel model token latency, and flag any SDK compatibility warning emitted at client side for telemetry aggregation.
risks: Misalignment between SDK owners and runtime maintainers could allow unsupported pairings to be published to customers
Insufficient perf telemetry coverage for certain enterprise customers (Dedicated) may produce false negatives for rollout gates
Automation bugs in CI validators could block legitimate minor updates if schema edge-cases are missed
